data.name: Damos
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Damos is derived from the word ‘damazo’, which means ‘to tame’ or ‘to conquer’. This name may have been given to a child born to parents who had successfully tamed wild animals or conquered their enemies. In the Bible, there is no direct mention of a figure named Damos, but it is a strong and symbolic name for a boy in Christian tradition.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name with strong connotations of courage and determination. Damos embodies the spirit of overcoming challenges and conquering fears.
data.numerology_meaning: A name that represents nurturing, caring, and serving others. Damos is a name for those who are compassionate and love to help others.

in_hebrew.name: דמוס
in_hebrew.meaning: דמוס הוא שם שפירושו עממי או ראוי לעם
in_hebrew.long_meaning: דמוס הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית ופירושו עממי או ראוי לעם, ויכול להיות קשור למונח 'דמוס' ביוונית שפירושו עם או קהל. השם דמוס עשוי להיות קשור גם למושג של שירות או הקדשה לעם או לקהילה.

in_greek.name: Δάμος
in_greek.meaning: Δάμος σημαίνει δημοκρατικός ή του λαού
in_greek.long_meaning: Δάμος είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'δᾶμος' (dāmos), που σημαίνει λαός ή πλήθος, και συνδέεται με την έννοια του δημοκρατικού ή του λαού. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, το όνομα Δάμος μπορεί να συσχετίζεται με την έννοια της υπηρεσίας προς τον λαό ή την κοινότητα.

in_latin.name: Damos

in_latin.long_meaning: The name Damos originates from Greek and Latin roots, signifying a person who is worthy of the people or related to the common folk. Historically, the term 'demos' in Greek denoted the common people or populace, suggesting a connection to democratic ideals or community service.

in_english.name: Damos
in_english.meaning: Damos means a person worthy of the people or community
in_english.long_meaning: The Christian name Damos originates from Greek roots, specifically from the word 'demos', meaning people or populace. This name signifies a person who is worthy of the people or community, reflecting values of service, humility, and connection to the common good. Historically, the concept of 'demos' was central to ancient Greek democracy, emphasizing the role of the people in governance. In a Christian context, Damos could symbolize a servant-leader or a figure devoted to the welfare of others.

data.cultural_impact: The name Damos carries a sense of strength and courage. It suggests a proud and valiant heritage, one of overcoming adversity and achieving greatness. Historically, names were often given to reflect the circumstances of a child's birth or the accomplishments of their parents. Damos is a name that would have been highly valued in ancient Greek or Roman societies, as it reflected the power and resilience of its bearer. In Christian tradition, this name continues to evoke a sense of perseverance and victory.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Damos can also be seen as a reminder of the spiritual power to tame and conquer the passions of the soul. As St. Paul reminds us, "I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength" (Phil. 4:13). Just as Damos may have symbolized the taming of wild beasts or the conquering of enemies in ancient times, our spiritual lives call us to tame our own negative emotions and thoughts and to conquer the temptations that can lead us away from God. In this way, the name Damos encourages us to be warriors for Christ, to stand firm in our faith, and to persevere in our spiritual journeys.

He is known for his role in the story of the Golden Ass, where he helps the protagonist Lucius transform into an ass and later aids in his restoration to human form.
